analysis:
The changed file is a Swift test harness, provider-swift/Tests/ClusterPlacementChecks/PlacementSetupCheck.swift. The only patch hunk is at head lines ~1260-1264. It adds a `publicModels: []` argument to `ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine` in a check labelled "records only, no public declaration". The supplied units cover base lines 334-952, which contain no changed lines. I examined those lines for context: placement, served-speed build scoping, qualification records and the owner-pilot flow. All of it is test fixtures with synthetic hashes and 192.0.2.x addresses, and it contains no secrets. There is no production code change, no change to trust boundaries, and no new attack surface.

The test change suggests that the production `publicTrafficLine` signature now takes a `publicModels` declaration. A public-traffic claim may therefore require a separate declaration in addition to qualification records. That is the more conservative direction, and it relates to the T-054 and T-052 themes (qualification evidence versus serving permission). The production implementation of `publicTrafficLine` is not in the supplied evidence. The reviewer cannot confirm that it fails closed when `publicModels` is empty or omitted, nor that other callers pass the correct list. The visible test only asserts that an empty list yields `notYetQualified` for a family with no passing record and a "qualified" prefix for the hand-off family, which is consistent with records still sufficing in that case. A later pass should check the production source for this default and for caller behavior.

I see no regression in the supplied evidence, and no threat-model gap caused by this change.
